title: Perfect complexes form a thick subcategory
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. In D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]: (1) if K\to L\to M\to K[1] is a distinguished triangle and two of K, L, M are perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], then so is the third; (2) if K\oplus L is perfect, then K and L are perfect; (3) shifts and finite direct sums of perfect objects are perfect.

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle, the two-out-of-three assertion is exactly Tag 08CR, applied to the three objects K, L, and M.
The direct-summand assertion is Tag 08CS, applied to the decomposition K ≅ L ⊕ M; it gives perfectness of each summand.

For shifts, reuse the existing proved private theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.perfect_shift from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectTwoOutOfThree, made available in proof bodies by a non-public import all. No duplicate shift theorem is introduced. Zero is represented on the whole space by the explicit zero complex; each term retracts into the rank-zero free sheaf. Perfectness is invariant under isomorphisms by the existing proved private perfect_of_iso theorem, also accessible through import all; it composes local representative isomorphisms. Binary biproducts are perfect by applying the middle-term two-out-of-three clause to Mathlib binaryBiproductTriangle_distinguished. These give closure under binary products and the empty product. ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts.mk' then gives finite-product closure. Apply prop_of_isLimit_fan to biproduct.isLimit K to obtain the finite-biproduct clause for arbitrary Finite I.

lean.statement: theorem perfect_thick_closure (X : Scheme.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] : (∀ (T : Triangle (schemeDerivedCategory X)), T ∈ distTriang (schemeDerivedCategory X) → (IsPerfect X T.obj₁ → IsPerfect X T.obj₂ → IsPerfect X T.obj₃) ∧ (IsPerfect X T.obj₂ → IsPerfect X T.obj₃ → IsPerfect X T.obj₁) ∧ (IsPerfect X T.obj₁ → IsPerfect X T.obj₃ → IsPerfect X T.obj₂)) ∧ (∀ (K L : schemeDerivedCategory X), IsPerfect X (K ⊞ L) → IsPerfect X K ∧ IsPerfect X L) ∧ (∀ (K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (n : ℤ), IsPerfect X K → IsPerfect X (K⟦n⟧)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type v) [Finite I] (K : I → schemeDerivedCategory X), (∀ i : I, IsPerfect X (K i)) → IsPerfect X (⨁ K))
